symptoms: Write failures with 'no space left on device'
Application crashes silently
Log files stop being written
Docker operations fail (pull, build, run)
common_causes: Application writing to container storage instead of volume
resolution_steps: Check disk usage: df -h and identify critical partitions at 90%+
Find large directories: du -sh /* | sort -rh
Check Docker: docker system df to find oversized containers/images
Clean old logs: find /var/log -type f -mtime +30 -delete
Remove Docker artifacts: docker system prune -a --volumes
Verify log rotation: logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/*
Extend partition or add volume if permanent fix needed
prevention_steps: Configure logrotate to rotate logs daily and compress old ones
Set up cron job to clean /tmp weekly
Enable Docker log rotation in daemon.json with maxsize and maxfile
Monitor disk usage regularly with prometheus or similar

symptoms: Service restarts unexpectedly with no error in application logs
System becomes unresponsive intermittently
Docker container exits with code 137 (SIGKILL)
dmesg shows OOM killer invoked
common_causes: Container memory limit too low for workload
Multiple services competing for limited RAM
Kernel OOM killer evicting processes as last resort
resolution_steps: Check OOM history: dmesg | grep -i oom | tail -20
Identify memory usage: ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -10
Monitor memory over time: watch -n 1 free -h
Check container limits: docker inspect <container> | grep -i memory
Increase container memory limit in docker-compose.yml
Profile the application for memory leaks (language-specific tools)
Restart service to clear memory (temporary fix while investigating leak)
prevention_steps: Set memory reservations in docker-compose to leave headroom
Enable memory metrics and alerts at 75%, 85%, 95% thresholds
Regular profiling for memory leaks in code reviews
Right-size container memory limits based on actual usage

symptoms: Application becomes slow, requests timeout
High load average (>number of CPU cores)
Response times spike even with same request volume
CPU usage climbs gradually or suddenly to 90-100%
common_causes: CPU-bound workload (database query, image processing, compilation)
Too many concurrent connections competing for CPU
No request queue limits causing runaway concurrency
resolution_steps: Identify hot process: top -n 1 -b | head -20
Check load: uptime and compare to nproc (number of cores)
Check what process is consuming: ps aux | grep <top_process_pid>
Reduce concurrency: tune worker count, connection pool size
Enable profiling to find hot code paths
For database: run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on slow queries, add indexes
Scale horizontally: add more instances behind load balancer
prevention_steps: Set reasonable concurrency limits in application config
Monitor CPU and latency metrics continuously
Add circuit breaker to shed load when CPU > threshold
Profile applications regularly for efficiency

symptoms: Application error: 'too many connections' or 'connection pool exhausted'
New requests hang or timeout waiting for connection
Service degrades under load but not resource-limited
Connection count reaches configured limit
common_causes: Configured connection pool too small for concurrent load
Connections not being properly closed or returned
Slow backend holding connections longer than expected
Sudden spike in concurrent users without scaling
resolution_steps: Check current connections: mysql -e 'SHOW PROCESSLIST;'
Count established connections: netstat -an | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
Identify idle connections: look for sleep status in PROCESSLIST
Kill stale connections: KILL <pid> for idle processes
Increase pool size: max_connections parameter (requires restart)
Enable connection pooling middleware: PgBouncer, ProxySQL
Reduce backend latency to free up connections faster
prevention_steps: Right-size connection pool based on concurrent load forecast
Implement connection timeout to close idle connections
Monitor connection pool utilization continuously
Use context managers or finally blocks to ensure connection return

symptoms: Service exits abruptly
Error visible in application logs (stderr/exceptions)
Process state is 'exited' but should be running
Requests fail immediately with no response
common_causes: Null pointer exception or index out of bounds
Uncaught signal or missing signal handler
Missing or incompatible dependency at runtime
Invalid configuration data causing startup failure
resolution_steps: Inspect logs: docker logs --tail 50 <container>
Check exit code: echo $? (non-zero = error)
Review recent changes: git log -5 --oneline
Validate configuration syntax: python -m json.tool config.json
Run locally to reproduce the issue
Add better error handling and validation in code
Deploy fixed version
prevention_steps: Add comprehensive error handling at service boundaries
Validate configuration on startup before using
Use type checking and linters to catch errors before runtime
Add structured logging with context for debugging

symptoms: Service running but not responding to requests
curl to service times out after connection
Process exists but shows 0% CPU in top
No new log entries for extended period
common_causes: Deadlock between threads/processes accessing shared resources
Blocked waiting for external resource (database, network)
Infinite loop or busy-wait consuming resources
resolution_steps: Check responsiveness: curl -v --max-time 5 http://<service>
Verify process exists: ps aux | grep <service>
Check system calls: strace -p <pid> to see what's blocking
Look at thread state: jstack (Java) or similar for your language
Restart service: docker restart <container>
Review recent code changes for lock/synchronization issues
Increase timeout on client side as temporary fix
prevention_steps: Use timeouts on all blocking operations
Add watchdog timers to detect hangs
Implement health check endpoints
Use tools like ThreadDump or strace for production debugging

symptoms: Container/service restarts every 2-10 seconds
Never stabilizes or reaches healthy state
Restart count climbs rapidly
Service port unreachable despite process appearing to run
common_causes: Database not ready when application starts
resolution_steps: Check restart count: docker inspect <container> | grep RestartCount
Review logs for pattern: docker logs <container> | tail -50
Verify secrets: docker inspect <container> | grep -i env | grep -i secret
Check startup order in docker-compose: depends_on, restart_policy
Add startup delay: sleep 10 before app starts
Implement health check: wait for dependencies before continuing
Increase restart grace period: stop_grace_period: 30s
prevention_steps: Use docker-compose depends_on with condition: service_healthy
Implement proper health checks for all services
Use explicit startup scripts that wait for dependencies
Add exponential backoff to restart policy

symptoms: Application error: 'connection refused' or 'could not connect to database'
Telnet to database port fails
Database query returns immediately with error, no data
common_causes: Database service not running or crashed
Database listening on wrong IP/port or localhost only
Network isolation (containers on different Docker networks)
Firewall blocking traffic between application and database
Database hung or out of resources
resolution_steps: Verify database running: docker ps | grep database
Check if listening: netstat -tlnp | grep <port> or lsof -i :<port>
Test connectivity: telnet <host> <port>
Check docker network: docker network inspect bridge
Verify connection string in app config
Restart database: docker restart <database>
Check database logs: docker logs <database> | tail -20
prevention_steps: Use docker-compose to manage network dependencies automatically
Add startup health checks for database connectivity
Log connection details for debugging
Use connection retry logic with exponential backoff

symptoms: Application crashes or behaves incorrectly
Service connects to wrong database/API endpoint
Logs show undefined variable or null value
Feature silently doesn't work (authentication, payment, etc.)
common_causes: .env file not loaded or not sourced in startup script
Variable name typo in application or config
Environment variable not passed through docker-compose
Secrets not mounted or not available
Configuration changed but containers not redeployed
resolution_steps: List environment: docker inspect <container> | grep -A 100 Env
Check expected vars: compare against docker-compose.yml
Verify secrets mounted: docker exec <container> ls -la /run/secrets/
Test variable: docker exec <container> echo $VAR_NAME
Rebuild and redeploy: docker-compose up -d --force-recreate
Check docker-compose for typos in variable names
prevention_steps: Use env-file in docker-compose to load from .env
Validate environment on startup and fail early if missing
Use schema/type checking for configuration
Print non-sensitive config on startup for debugging

symptoms: Service fails to start with parse or validation error
Error message includes line number of config file
Service won't start even though binary exists and is executable
resolution_steps: Validate syntax: python -m json.tool config.json
Or use yq: yq eval config.yaml
Check error line number and review that section
Compare against template or working configuration
Check git diff for recent changes: git diff config.yaml
Roll back to known-good configuration
prevention_steps: Use editor with syntax checking and auto-format
Validate configuration on startup before using
Include example/template config in repository
Use schema validation (JSON Schema, etc.)

symptoms: HTTPS connections fail with certificate error
Browser shows 'not secure' or certificate warning
curl shows 'certificate verify failed'
Application error: 'SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED'
common_causes: Certificate domain doesn't match requested domain
Self-signed certificate not in client trust store
Certificate not installed or mounted in container
resolution_steps: Check expiry: openssl s_client -connect host:443 | grep notAfter
Or: echo | openssl s_client -servername example.com -connect example.com:443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates
Renew certificate: certbot renew (for Let's Encrypt)
For self-signed: add to trust store or disable verification (dev only)
Restart web server: docker restart nginx
Verify mounted: docker inspect <container> | grep -i volume | grep cert
prevention_steps: Set up certificate renewal automation (certbot auto-renew)
Monitor certificate expiry dates with alerts 30 days before
Use Let's Encrypt with auto-renewal for free certificates
Include certificate info in deployment verification

pattern_name: Docker Image Pull Failure / Registry Authentication
symptoms: Cannot start container, error during image pull
Error: 'image not found' or 'no such image'
Error: 'unauthorized: authentication required'
docker pull fails with same error
common_causes: Image tag doesn't exist in registry
Disk full (no space to download image)
resolution_steps: Verify image exists: docker search <image>
For private registry: docker login <registry>
Check credentials: cat ~/.docker/config.json
Manually pull to test: docker pull <image>:<tag>
Check disk space: df -h /var/lib/docker
Update docker-compose with correct image name and tag
Verify network connectivity to registry
prevention_steps: Use image digests instead of tags for production
Implement image pull in CI/CD before deployment
Monitor registry availability and quotas
Use private registries for internal images with auth

symptoms: Cannot reach service by hostname: 'name or service not known'
nslookup or dig shows SERVFAIL or NXDOMAIN
Works with IP but not with hostname
Specific queries fail while others succeed
common_causes: DNS server not responding or unreachable
resolution_steps: Test DNS: nslookup 8.8.8.8 (works?) then test hostname
Check resolver: cat /etc/resolv.conf
For docker: docker exec <container> nslookup <hostname>
Query specific server: dig @8.8.8.8 <hostname>
Flush local cache: systemctl restart systemd-resolved
Verify DNS record exists: dig <hostname> +short
Use IP address as temporary workaround
prevention_steps: Configure stable DNS servers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1)
Monitor DNS resolution times
Use internal DNS (like systemd-resolved) with fallback
Validate DNS records in CI/CD before deployment

pattern_name: Port Already in Use / Binding Conflict
symptoms: Service fails to start: 'address already in use'
Error: 'bind: permission denied' (port < 1024 without root)
netstat shows port in use by another process
Port shows in TIME_WAIT state
common_causes: Another service already using the port
Previous instance not cleanly shut down (TIME_WAIT)
Trying to bind privileged port (< 1024) without root
resolution_steps: Find process using port: lsof -i :<port>
Kill it: kill <pid>
Check for TIME_WAIT: netstat -tan | grep :<port>
Wait 60-120 seconds for TIME_WAIT to expire
Or use SO_REUSEADDR in application code
Change service port if available
Check docker-compose for duplicate port entries
prevention_steps: Use unique port numbers for each service
Implement graceful shutdown with SO_REUSEADDR
Use dynamic port assignment in tests
Document port assignments in docker-compose

symptoms: Requests to remote service timeout or 'no route to host'
ping to host fails or very slow
curl connection times out
common_causes: Remote host down or network unreachable
resolution_steps: Test connectivity: ping <host>
Check routing: ip route and traceroute <host>
Inspect firewall: iptables -L -n or cloud firewall rules
Check network interface: ip link show
Test application port: curl -v <url> --max-time 5
For docker: check if containers on same network
Increase timeout on client (temporary)
prevention_steps: Monitor reachability to critical services
Configure reasonable timeouts (5-30s depending on service)
Use circuit breaker to fail fast
Document network topology and dependencies

pattern_name: Reverse Proxy / Load Balancer Not Routing
symptoms: Frontend can't reach backend service
Nginx/Apache shows 'upstream timed out'
External requests fail but local requests work
nginx -t shows error in config
common_causes: Proxy config has wrong backend address
resolution_steps: Validate nginx config: nginx -t
Check backend health: curl http://<backend>:<port>
Verify proxy running: ps aux | grep nginx
Restart proxy: systemctl restart nginx
Check firewall: iptables -L -n (between proxy and backend)
Review config for IP/port typos
Check logs: tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log
prevention_steps: Test backend connectivity in health checks
Monitor upstream availability
Log proxy errors with timestamps
Use monitoring for backend response times

symptoms: Database fails to start with 'invalid page header' or 'checksum failed'
Database process exits immediately
Cannot query database even though it's running
resolution_steps: Check logs: docker logs <database>
For PostgreSQL: pg_resetwal to reset WAL
For MySQL: innodb_recovery startup flag
For SQLite: .recover command
Check filesystem: fsck -n <device> (read-only)
Restore from backup if recovery fails
Verify hardware with SMART tests
prevention_steps: Regular backups before system changes
Use filesystems with journaling
Implement clean shutdown procedures
Monitor filesystem health with SMART

symptoms: Queries taking seconds to complete
Application hangs during database operations
High disk I/O and CPU during queries
Response times spike without change in load
common_causes: Missing index on frequently queried column
Full table scan instead of indexed lookup
resolution_steps: Enable slow query log
Analyze query plan: EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT ...
Look for sequential scans without index
Add index: CREATE INDEX idx_col ON table(col);
Update statistics: ANALYZE table;
Check for locks: SHOW PROCESSLIST;
Kill blocking transaction if needed
prevention_steps: Monitor slow query log continuously
Profile queries in development
Add indexes for common queries
Regular statistics updates (ANALYZE)

symptoms: Cannot create files even though df shows free space
Error: 'No space left on device' from touch/create
df -i shows 100% usage
common_causes: Too many small files (millions of log entries, temp files)
resolution_steps: Check inode usage: df -i
Find high inode dirs: du --inodes -s /* | sort -rn
Remove old small files: find /var/log -type f -mtime +30 -delete
Clean temp: rm -rf /tmp/* (if safe)
Configure log rotation to prevent recurrence
Migrate to filesystem with more inodes
prevention_steps: Monitor inode usage regularly
Configure log rotation and cleanup
Set up alerts when inode usage > 80%

symptoms: Mount point missing or data unavailable
Application fails because expected directory doesn't exist
ls on mount point shows empty when should have data
resolution_steps: Check fstab: cat /etc/fstab
Try manual mount: mount <device> <mountpoint>
Check device exists: lsblk or ls -la /dev/
For NFS: check server reachable, credentials correct
Repair filesystem: fsck <device> (unmounted)
Restore from backup if data corrupted
prevention_steps: Document all mounts and verify regularly
Test mount on startup with health checks
Keep backups of critical mounted data

symptoms: Application gets 'permission denied' when accessing volume
ls -la shows volume owned by root with restrictive perms
Application runs as non-root user but can't write
common_causes: Volume owner is root, app runs as non-root user
Container user UID doesn't match host UID
resolution_steps: Check ownership: ls -la /volume
Fix owner: chown -R 1000:1000 /volume
Fix permissions: chmod 755 /volume
Or: run app as root at startup, fix perms, switch user
Verify in container: docker exec <container> ls -la /volume
prevention_steps: Use consistent UIDs across host and containers
Set volume ownership explicitly in docker-compose
Document volume mount requirements

symptoms: Suspicious activity in logs, unexpected resource usage
Unusual processes running, malicious behavior
Failed login attempts spike
Unrecognized connections or data access
common_causes: Credentials leaked (committed to git, exposed in logs)
resolution_steps: Rotate all credentials immediately
Check git history: git log -p | grep -i password
Kill suspicious processes: pkill -f <process>
Review logs: tail -f /var/log/auth.log
Run updates: apt update && apt upgrade
Restrict access: firewall rules or ssh config
Consider full system reinstall if severe
prevention_steps: Never commit credentials to git
Use secrets management (Docker secrets, Vault)
Rotate credentials regularly
Monitor for unusual activity with IDS/logs

symptoms: Credentials visible in application logs
Secrets readable in docker inspect output
Passwords in git history or docker-compose
resolution_steps: Search for exposed secrets: grep -r 'password\|token\|key' /var/log/
Disable debug logging: LOG_LEVEL=INFO
Use secrets management: Docker secrets, HashiCorp Vault
Mask secrets in logs: custom formatter
Rotate any exposed secrets
Redact log files
Check git history: git log -p | grep -i password
prevention_steps: Use secrets management from day 1
Configure logging to mask sensitive fields
Code review for secret exposure
Pre-commit hooks to block credential commits

symptoms: Process memory grows over hours/days
Eventually crashes with OOM
Memory usage sawtooth pattern (GC can't keep up)
resolution_steps: Monitor memory over time: watch -n 5 'ps aux | head -20'
Profile memory: language-specific tools (jmap, memory_profiler)
Review recent code changes
Increase memory temporarily while fixing
Implement periodic restart as short-term fix
Deploy fix with memory profiling
prevention_steps: Regular memory profiling in development
Use memory leak detection tools in CI
Code review for resource lifetime issues
Monitor production memory metrics

symptoms: Requests taking much longer than baseline
p95/p99 latency spiked
Users report slowness
resolution_steps: Profile request timing: curl -w '@curl-format.txt' <url>
Identify where time is spent (database, network, processing)
Enable query slow log
Check resources: top, iostat -x 1 5
Optimize hot path: cache, index, parallel
Scale horizontally if resource-limited
prevention_steps: Monitor latency p95/p99 continuously
Profile critical paths in development
Set latency budgets and alert on violations

pattern_name: Docker Container Out of Disk Space
symptoms: Docker operations fail
Application writes fail
Logs show 'no space left on device'
docker run fails to create container
resolution_steps: Check host disk: df -h /var/lib/docker
Check container size: docker system df
Clean container logs: docker exec <container> rm /var/log/*
Configure log rotation: daemon.json
Prune unused images: docker system prune -a
Increase host disk if needed
prevention_steps: Configure Docker log rotation
Monitor /var/lib/docker disk usage
Set up alerts when disk > 80%
Use volumes for application logs

pattern_name: Docker Network Isolation / Container Can't Reach Service
symptoms: Container can't reach another container by hostname
ping between containers fails
Network unreachable error
common_causes: DNS service not working in container
resolution_steps: Check networks: docker network ls
Inspect network: docker network inspect <network>
List containers on network: docker network inspect bridge
Test connectivity: docker exec <container> ping <other>
Create network: docker network create <name>
Reconnect: docker network connect <network> <container>
prevention_steps: Use docker-compose: networks automatically created
Define explicit networks for service groups
Test network connectivity in CI

symptoms: docker stop hangs for 10 seconds then force kills
No graceful shutdown message in logs
Service doesn't get SIGTERM signal
common_causes: PID 1 not properly set (shell script wrapper)
resolution_steps: Implement signal handling in application
Ensure PID 1 is app: use exec in entrypoint
Test locally: kill -TERM <pid>
Increase grace period: stop_grace_period: 30s
Kill explicitly if needed: docker kill <container>
prevention_steps: Implement proper signal handling in all apps
Use exec in Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT
Test graceful shutdown in CI
Document shutdown sequence

symptoms: docker ps fails with 'Cannot connect to daemon'
systemctl status docker shows failed
Docker commands hang or timeout
resolution_steps: Restart daemon: systemctl restart docker
Check disk: df -h /var/lib/docker
Clean corrupted state: docker system prune -a (caution)
Check file descriptors: ulimit -n (increase if < 8192)
Review logs: journalctl -u docker -f
prevention_steps: Monitor Docker daemon health
Set up disk usage alerts
Monitor file descriptor usage
Regular cleanup: docker system prune

symptoms: Calls to external API timeout
HTTP 429 responses (rate limited)
Service degrades when calling external APIs
resolution_steps: Check external service status page
Implement exponential backoff for retries
Cache responses: don't repeat same query
Add timeout: curl --max-time 5
Contact API provider for rate limit increase
Implement circuit breaker pattern
prevention_steps: Monitor external API response times
Implement timeouts on all external calls
Use caching to reduce API calls
Have fallback/degraded mode

symptoms: Webhooks not being received
Notifications not sent
Events lost when endpoint unavailable
resolution_steps: Verify endpoint reachable: curl -X POST <url>
Increase timeout if needed
Reduce payload size
Verify authentication headers
Implement idempotency: handle duplicates
Add retry logic with exponential backoff
prevention_steps: Implement idempotency keys
Persistent webhook queue (don't lose)
Health checks for webhook endpoints
Monitoring for delivery failures

symptoms: Service won't start, 'dependency failed' error
systemctl status shows failed
Manual execution works but systemd launch fails
common_causes: ExecStart path wrong or executable missing
Permission denied (service user can't access file)
resolution_steps: Check status: systemctl status <service>
Review logs: journalctl -u <service> -n 20
Verify path: which <executable>
Check dependencies: systemctl status <dependency>
Fix and reload: systemctl daemon-reload
Check permissions: service user can access files
prevention_steps: Document service dependencies
Test systemd startup in CI
Use dependency management in unit files
Monitor service startup times
